args.title: deviation-analysis-memo.docx
args.body:
DEVIATION ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet — Counterparty Markup Review
Banking & Finance Practice

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

Engagement: banking-finance analyze — Counterparty Markup Deviation Analysis of Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet
Output: deviation-analysis-memo.docx

I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This memorandum compares the lender's markup (the "Counterparty Markup") of the Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet (the "Original Term Sheet" or "Base Materials") against the base provisions, cross-referencing the controlling partner instructions and the applicable financial data and schedules, and identifies every material deviation introduced by the counterparty. Each deviation is reconciled against the base materials, the disclosure schedules, and the deal-team instruction, with a recommended position for the client.

Consistent with the engagement instruction, this analysis relies on (i) the operative base materials, (ii) the deal-team partner instructions (as revised by the controlling, most recent message), and (iii) the financial data set forth in the disclosure schedules and exhibits. It does not rely on the Northgale commercial contracting playbook that is misfiled in the matter folder; that document belongs to an unrelated deep-drafting/Northgale engagement and is expressly excluded from this analysis.

II. BASE MATERIALS AND CONTROLLING SOURCES

A. Base provisions. The Original Term Sheet contains, among other things, representations and warranties, affirmative and negative covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions. Three clusters of provisions are implicated by the Counterparty Markup: (1) the indemnification mechanics (cap and basket), (2) the Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") definition, and (3) the survival period for the core representations.

B. Disclosure schedules and financial data. The following schedules and exhibit qualify and, where applicable, control over general statements in the base materials:
   • Schedule 3.7 — discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that directly intersect the MAE carve-outs introduced in the Counterparty Markup.
   • Schedule 5.2 — lists retained liabilities that the Counterparty Markup's indemnification changes would silently shift.
   • Exhibit B — sets the survival matrix for the representations, which the Counterparty Markup's limitation-period change contradicts.
   Under the base materials, scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the term sheet.

C. Controlling partner instructions. The deal-team partner email thread on this engagement is the controlling source for negotiation posture. The most recent message REVISES the prior priorities and states:
   • The client will CONCEDE the basket conversion (i.e., the conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket).
   • The client treats ANY reduction in the survival period as a WALK-AWAY issue.
   Only the latest message controls; the earlier, superseded message stating the opposite ordering does not apply.

III. DEVIATIONS IDENTIFIED IN THE COUNTERPARTY MARKUP

Deviation 1 — Indemnification: silent reduction of the cap and conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

   Description. The Counterparty Markup (i) silently reduces the indemnification cap relative to the Original Term Sheet and (ii) converts the indemnification basket from a deductible into a tipping basket.

   Reconciliation to base materials and financial data. Under the base materials the basket operates as a deductible, meaning the client retains first-dollar exposure and the counterparty's obligation attaches only above the threshold. Converting to a tipping basket means that, once the threshold is crossed, the counterparty becomes liable for the full amount from the first dollar. This materially increases potential recovery and, combined with the listed retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2, could silently shift a meaningful portion of retained liability back onto the indemnifying party. The cap reduction further narrows the indemnifying party's aggregate exposure, which interacts adversely with the retained-liability profile on Schedule 5.2.

   Position. Consistent with the controlling partner instruction, the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket). The reduction of the indemnification cap, however, is a separate and material deviation that is NOT covered by the basket-concession instruction. The cap should be restored to the original term sheet level, or, at a minimum, the retained liabilities disclosed on Schedule 5.2 must be expressly carved out of any reduced cap. Recommend countering to reinstate the original cap.

Deviation 2 — Material Adverse Effect: addition of carve-outs for regulatory action.

   Description. The Counterparty Markup expands the definition of Material Adverse Effect to add carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."

   Reconciliation to base materials and financial data. Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries involving the borrower. By carving out regulatory action of precisely that character, the markup would exclude from the definition of MAE the very adverse regulatory developments that the client has reason to expect from the two pending inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7. The carve-out would therefore deprive the client of an MAE trigger for a material, foreseeable regulatory outcome, undercutting the protective function of the MAE representation as set in the base materials. As the scheduled exceptions control, the pending inquiries must be treated as covered by the MAE definition.

   Position. The MAE carve-outs should be REJECTED in their current form. At a minimum, the carve-out must be narrowed so that it cannot operate to exempt the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 from constituting an MAE. Recommend countering to (i) delete the regulatory-action carve-out, or (ii) expressly provide that the carve-out does not apply to the Schedule 3.7 inquiries.

Deviation 3 — Survival: new limitation period shortening survival for the core representations.

   Description. The Counterparty Markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations relative to the base materials.

   Reconciliation to base materials and financial data. Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the representations in the Original Term Sheet. The markup's shortened limitation period contradicts that matrix, cutting off the client's ability to pursue claims for breaches of the core representations after a reduced period. Survival is a threshold protection on the enforceability of every representation-based claim, and any reduction directly erodes the client's remedies under the credit facility.

   Position. Under the controlling partner instruction, ANY reduction in the survival period is a WALK-AWAY issue. The shortened limitation period must therefore be treated as a non-negotiable rejection point. Recommend rejecting any reduction to the survival periods set forth in Exhibit B and restoring the survival matrix in full.

IV. SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDED POSITIONS

   1. Basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket): CONCEDE, per controlling partner instruction.
   2. Indemnification cap reduction: REJECT / COUNTER to reinstate the original cap; ensure Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities are not silently absorbed by any reduced cap.
   3. MAE regulatory-action carve-outs: REJECT / COUNTER to narrow so the two Schedule 3.7 pending regulatory inquiries remain a valid MAE trigger.
   4. Survival-period reduction: WALK-AWAY issue; reject any shortening of the Exhibit B survival matrix.

V. CONCLUSION

The Counterparty Markup introduces three material deviations. The basket conversion may be conceded per the partner's controlling direction; the indemnification cap reduction and the MAE carve-outs should be countered to preserve the client's protections, including the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities and the Schedule 3.7 regulatory exposure; and any survival-period reduction is a walk-away item per the controlling instruction and must be rejected outright. The Northgale playbook that is misfiled in the matter folder was identified as belonging to an unrelated engagement and was not relied upon in this analysis.

Prepared in reliance on the base materials, the disclosure schedules and financial data, and the controlling partner instruction.
